title: Week 3, part 1 · Classical classifiers by hand

lines: Week three works everything out by hand on one tiny corpus. Learn these numbers: the exam has no calculator.
Two positive reviews: good good movie, and good movie. Two negative reviews: bad bad movie, and bad movie.
Four documents, three word types, ten tokens, and five tokens in each class.
Fit the vocabulary and the I D F on the training set only. Calling fit on the test set leaks it into your features.
Naive Bayes uses two different denominators. The prior counts documents: two out of four, so zero point five.
The word probabilities count tokens, with add-one smoothing: count plus one, over five tokens plus three word types.
Good in the positive class: three plus one over eight, one half. Good in the negative class: one over eight.
Now classify good movie. Positive: one half, times one half, times three eighths. Negative: one half, times one eighth, times three eighths.
Divide by the sum: positive gets zero point eight. That is the model's probability, not its accuracy.
Logistic regression. Features good and bad are two and zero, weights zero point eight and minus one, bias minus zero point four.
z is zero point eight times two, plus zero, minus zero point four: one point two.
The sigmoid of one point two is about zero point seven seven, so predict positive.
Training uses cross-entropy, and its gradient is simply p minus y, times x.
Here that is zero point seven seven minus one, times two, so the weight goes up. And when every feature is zero, the bias still learns.
The SVM scores f of x equals good minus bad, and multiplies by the label to get the margin.
A negative review with good one and bad two: f is minus one, the label is minus one, so the margin is one.
The hinge loss is the larger of zero and one minus the margin. Margin one gives loss zero.
A positive review with score zero point five is on the right side, but inside the margin, so it still costs zero point five.
Where do these classifiers fail? Word order.
With unigrams, not good has the word good with a positive weight, so z is plus zero point four: positive. Wrong.
Add the bigram not good as its own feature with weight minus one point two, and z drops to minus zero point eight: negative.
Changing the classifier does not help. Only a representation that keeps the order can.
